newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka pushes for more tea sales to Iran.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka pushes for more tea sales to Iran.

text.p: Sri Lanka wants Teheran to increase imports of tea as part of its aim to cut its rising trade deficit with Iran, a government minister said.

Sri Lankan Trade Minister Kingsley Wickramaratne said on Friday that tea exports to Iran fell to 6,000 tonnes in 1995 from a high of 32,000 tonnes in 1991 after Teheran began sourcing the commodity from Kenya.
"The dominant share we enjoyed a couple of years ago has been overtaken by other sources," Wickramaratne told a meeting of Sri Lanka-Iran Joint Economic Commission in Colombo.
He said though tea exports to Iran had risen to 10,000 tonnes last year, it was not significant considering Iran's total tea imports.
A trade ministry statement said Kenya's tea exports to Iran had risen sharply to 12,000 tonnes last year from a mere 200 tonnes in 1995.

Total trade between the two countries was worth 10.4 billion rupees ($179.4 million) in 1996, with trade balance in favour of Iran mostly due to large oil imports by Sri Lanka from that country, the statement said.
